newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shares end lower with funds on sidelines.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shares end lower with funds on sidelines.

text.p: Colombian stocks, led by Banco Ganadero, slipped on Wednesday, ending slightly lower as foreign funds steered clear of the market, traders said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed down by a razor-thin 0.07 percent at 18,408.53 on turnover of about two billion pesos. Bogota's IBB dropped 0.18 percent, ending at 1,202.33 on above-average trading volume of almost seven billion pesos.
In Bogota, Ganadero shares fell 0.50 percent to 395 pesos per share, accounting for most of the volume in the capital, as large shareholders carried out cross trades, brokers said.
Brokers attributed the absence of foreign funds to speculation about a possible devaluation of Brazil's currency.
"Funds invested in South America are waiting to see what's going on in Brazil," one trader said of the devaluation talk.
Among the declining issues, brewer Bavaria SA, which closed down 0.24 percent in Bogota at 8,180 pesos, and cigarette maker Coltabaco, which shed 1.19 percent in Bogota to end at 4,150 pesos.
